issues.description: Logic gate is too broad — disabling Enter swallows ALL non-Tab keys including arrows, Escape, navigation, and printable characters
issues.detail: The guard `if not get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` runs for every keystroke while the completion widget has focus. When the option is disabled, any key other than Tab (Up/Down arrows to navigate completions, Esc to dismiss, Backspace, letters, etc.) will hit `self.hide()` and forward the event to the textedit. This breaks completion-list navigation entirely and makes the popup unusable when the option is off. The intent was clearly to only intercept Enter/Return (and possibly Tab to keep accepting), so the condition should explicitly check for Key_Return/Key_Enter.

issues.description: Early-return placement bypasses important pre-conditions further down in keyPressEvent
issues.detail: The new block is inserted right after the `item = self.currentItem()` line but before the `if item is None: item = self.item(0)` fallback and the rest of the key handling. Even if narrowed to Return/Enter, the code returns before the broader keyPressEvent finishes, which may skip parent-class handling, modifier checks, or completion-state cleanup that the function normally performs. The fix needs to be scoped to the specific key branch (where Return/Enter is currently handled) rather than at the top of the dispatcher.

issues.description: get_conf called on every keypress — should be cached or read once
issues.detail: `self.get_conf('use_enter_for_completions', section='completions')` is invoked inside keyPressEvent, which fires on every key while the popup is open. Configuration reads typically go through the CONF manager and are not free. This value should be cached as an instance attribute updated via a config observer (apply_plugin_settings / on_conf_update) rather than re-read per keystroke.

issues.description: Forwarding keyPressEvent to textedit may double-handle or mishandle the event
issues.detail: `self.textedit.keyPressEvent(event)` is called directly after `self.hide()`. Depending on the Qt event propagation in Spyder's editor, this can cause re-entrancy issues (the textedit may itself trigger another completion request) and the event's `accept()` state isn't managed. Compare with how Escape or focus-out are handled elsewhere in the widget — typically hide() alone is sufficient and Qt routes the next event naturally.

issues.description: No tests added for the new behavior
issues.detail: A user-facing toggle that changes how Enter and Tab interact with the completion popup is exactly the kind of regression-prone behavior that benefits from a unit/integration test. Spyder has a tests directory for editor widgets; the PR adds neither a test for the enabled-True path nor for the disabled path. At minimum a parametrized test that simulates Enter/Tab with both settings would protect against the breadth-of-key-handling bug above.

issues.description: Style: `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` should be `key != Qt.Key_Tab`
issues.detail: PEP 8 / readability nit. `not key == ...` is harder to scan than `key != ...`. Spyder's coding style favors the direct comparison.

issues.description: Config default True preserves prior behavior but the option name is positively phrased while the UI tip describes the disabled state
issues.detail: The setting `use_enter_for_completions` defaults to True (Enter accepts), which is correct for backward compatibility. The tooltip phrases it negatively ('If this option is disabled, completions will be accepted with the Tab key only'), which is fine but could be clearer by also stating what is True does. Minor copy nit; not blocking.

issues.description: No config migration / version bump noted
issues.detail: Spyder's config system typically requires a CONF_VERSION bump when adding new keys to defaults so existing user configs pick up the new key. The diff only adds the key to `spyder/config/main.py` defaults; it doesn't appear to bump CONF_VERSION. If Spyder's defaults system handles missing keys at runtime via `get_conf` fallbacks this is fine, but worth a maintainer sanity check.

issues.description: Layout row 5 is now skipped — rows go 0,1,2,3,4 then 5 with no row 4 originally used but completions_hint_after_idle was at row 5 already
issues.detail: Pre-PR, completions_after_characters lived at row 3 and completions_hint_after_idle at row 5 (skipping 4). Post-PR, completions_after_characters moves to row 4, so the grid now correctly fills 0..5. This is actually cleaner — flagging only as informational since it's easy to mis-read the diff and think a row was skipped.

dissents.topic: Should the guard intercept only Enter/Return, or any non-Tab key?

positions.position: The author wrote `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` deliberately, implying any non-Tab key should dismiss the popup when the option is off. This matches a Tab-only acceptance model.

That interpretation breaks arrow-key navigation within the completion list and Escape-to-dismiss handling. The user-visible intent of the linked issue (#12728) is specifically about Enter being annoying — narrowing the check to Key_Return/Key_Enter is what users actually want. This is the correct reading and the current code is a bug.
Keystrokes occur at human speed (max ~10/s) and Spyder's CONF lookup is a dict access — not worth caching.
Spyder uses a configuration observer pattern elsewhere; reading config in a hot path is inconsistent with project conventions and can compound when many keypress handlers do the same.

dissents.topic: Where the guard should live in keyPressEvent

positions.position: Putting the check early is fine — it short-circuits before any other handling, which is exactly the desired effect when the option is disabled.

The existing keyPressEvent already has a branch that handles Enter/Return acceptance. The toggle belongs inside that branch so the rest of the popup keeps working (arrows, Esc, typing-through). This is the cleaner architectural fix.

review.summary: The PR adds a user-requested option to disable Enter-to-accept for code completions, which is a sensible feature. However the implementation has a likely-correctness bug: the guard `not get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` fires for ALL non-Tab keys when the option is off, which would break arrow-key navigation within the popup, Escape-to-dismiss, and any typing-through behavior — not just Enter. The check should be scoped to Qt.Key_Return / Qt.Key_Enter, and ideally moved inside the existing Enter/Return branch of keyPressEvent rather than placed as an early-return at the top. Secondary issues: get_conf is called on every keystroke (cache via observer), keyPressEvent forwarding to textedit risks re-entrancy, no tests were added, and the style nit `not key == X` should be `key != X`. The config default (True) correctly preserves existing behavior.
